equation_request.abstract: Continuous time quantum walks provide an important framework for designing new algorithms and modelling quantum transport and state transfer problems. Often, the graph representing the structure of a problem contains certain symmetries that confine the dynamics to a smaller subspace of the full Hilbert space. In this work, we use invariant subspace methods, that can be computed systematically using Lanczos algorithm, to obtain the reduced set of states that encompass the dynamics of the problem at hand without the specific knowledge of underlying symmetries. First, we apply this method to obtain new instances of graphs where the spatial quantum search algorithm is optimal: complete graphs with broken links and complete bipartite graphs, in particular, the star graph. These examples show that regularity and high-connectivity are not needed to achieve optimal spatial search. We also show that this method considerably simplifies the calculation of quantum transport efficiencies. Furthermore, we observe improved efficiencies by removing a few links from highly symmetric graphs. Finally, we show that this reduction method also allows us to obtain an upper bound for the fidelity of a single qubit transfer on an XY spin network.

specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk spatial search on a small graph with marked vertex w, H = -gamma*A - |w><w|. Use Lanczos from |s> to get a small Krylov subspace and reduced tridiagonal T, tune gamma and find t* maximizing |<w|e^{-iHt}|s>|^2, then simulate the walk on n qubits and read the marked-vertex probability.
specification.reconstruction_scope: ONE tiny instance: complete graph K_N with N=8 (n=3 qubits), marked vertex w=5 (binary 101), no ancilla, exact two-projector evolution. The star graph, broken-link complete graphs, transport efficiencies and XY-chain fidelity bound are outside scope and only sketched as Lanczos variants.

symbols.meaning: number of vertex qubits, ceil(log2 N)

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Hamiltonian of the walk with oracle term
equations.justification: Standard Childs-Goldstone CTQW search Hamiltonian; the abstract mentions spatial search but does not state H.

equations.label: Complete graph adjacency
equations.latex: A=N|s\rangle\langle s|-I,\quad H=-\gamma N|s\rangle\langle s|-|w\rangle\langle w|+\gamma I
equations.description: For K_N the adjacency is a rank-one projector up to identity; the identity gives only a global phase

equations.label: Lanczos recursion
equations.description: Classical Lanczos builds the Krylov basis and tridiagonal T; stops when beta=0 (d=2 for complete graph)
equations.abstract_quote: invariant subspace methods, that can be computed systematically using Lanczos algorithm
equations.justification: Abstract names Lanczos for the invariant subspace; the recursion itself is standard.
assumptions: Exact arithmetic or numerical tolerance for beta stop

equations.label: Reduced 2x2 resonance
equations.latex: \gamma=1/N:\ H_{red}\simeq -\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{1}\cdot c-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt N}\,\sigma_x\ \text{in basis }\{|w\rangle,|s_\perp\rangle\}\ (\text{up to diagonal shifts}),\ P_w(t)=\sin^2(t/\sqrt N)\ \text{(large-N approx.)}
equations.description: At resonance the two-level splitting gives P_w approx 1 at t ~ (pi/2) sqrt(N); finite N=8 has corrections, so use numerics from T
equations.justification: Known Childs-Goldstone result; asymptotic, not exact for N=8.
assumptions: Large-N approximation; for N=8 compute t* numerically from exact T

equations.label: Predicted success probability
equations.description: Reduced-space prediction in Krylov coordinates compared with simulation; the Krylov coordinate of |w> is its overlap expressed in the basis
equations.abstract_quote: to obtain the reduced set of states that encompass the dynamics of the problem at hand
equations.justification: Dynamics confined to Krylov space so reduced evolution reproduces the full amplitude.
assumptions: |w> lies in the Krylov space of |s> under H

equations.label: Exact circuit evolution
equations.latex: e^{-iHt}=e^{-i\gamma t}\,e^{i\gamma N t|s\rangle\langle s|}e^{it|w\rangle\langle w|}\ \text{(exact only if the projectors commute; otherwise use PauliEvolutionGate or Trotter)}
equations.description: Projectors do not commute, so Trotter product with r steps approximates; |s><s| = H^n X^n C^{n-1}Z X^n H^n phase form, |w><w| = multi-controlled phase with X conjugation on zero bits of w
equations.justification: Proposed construction; the product is only first-order Trotter, so tolerance is needed.
assumptions: Trotter steps r large enough, or use exact PauliEvolutionGate of the Pauli decomposition of H

registers.name: q
registers.role: vertex register, little-endian: vertex index = sum q_i 2^i

steps.description: Classically build A, H, run Lanczos from |s> to get T, d, and Krylov basis.
Set gamma=1/N (or tune numerically on T near the avoided crossing) and find t* maximizing P_w.
Prepare |s> with Hadamards and apply exp(-iHt*) via PauliEvolutionGate on the Pauli decomposition of H (exact) or Trotter with enough steps.
Measure all 3 qubits and compute P_w from counts for the bitstring of w, reading keys as reversed (last char is qubit 0).

specification.measurement: Measure all n qubits in computational basis; P_w = counts[bitstring of w]/shots, with Qiskit little-endian keys (w=5 -> '101').
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the estimated P_w with the Lanczos-reduced prediction in eq_5 within tolerance; gamma and t* chosen classically.
assumptions: N=8 complete graph, w=5 chosen as the smallest instance
Adjacency form of H, no black-box queries; oracle term is built explicitly from the known w
